For generations, we have been taught to live the same way every day. Same routines. Same expectations. Same pace, no matter the time of year or how we feel.

But nature has never worked like that. 

The seasons remind us that life moves in cycles. Expansion and contraction. Growth and rest. Energy and stillness. Our bodies are designed the same way.

Winter invites rest and replenishment. 

A time to conserve energy, nourish deeply and honour sleep.

Spring brings renewal. 

A gentle awakening that supports natural detox pathways and fresh beginnings.

Summer is abundant and outward. 

A season of vitality, connection, joy and movement.

Autumn encourages reflection and harvest. 

A moment to ground, strengthen immunity and prepare for the quieter months ahead.

Ancient practices like Ayurveda and Traditional Chinese Medicine have always honoured these rhythms. Not through extreme resets or rigid protocols, but through small, intuitive shifts that support the body as it moves through each phase.

When we stop resisting the seasons and start listening, wellness becomes less about discipline and more about relationship. A relationship with nature. With our bodies. With ourselves.

This wheel of the year is a reminder that you do not need to live at full speed all year long. You only need to live in rhythm.

Since 2018, Ancient + Brave has been immersed in the science of supplements. Eight years in the collagen space, backed by @dr_jenna_macciochi our Director of Science and Innovation, and her twenty plus years as an immunologist. Jenna and our Director of Nutrition & Education, @jo_woodhurst_nutrition share the one myth we’re tired of hearing.

The myth: you need Vitamin C in your collagen supplement for it to actually work.

You don’t. And this collagen misunderstanding has been amplified by marketing claims that have muddied the water considerably. 

Vitamin C contributes to normal collagen formation. That part is real, authorised and not in question. But the enzymes that use it work inside your cells, over hours, not in the second you drink your collagen in your morning tea or coffee. 

What actually matters is ensuring that you get enough Vitamin C in your diet. It’s simple as the equivalent of a kiwi or a handful of strawberries, alongside everything else whole fruits and vegetables brings alongside it.

Then there is heat. Collagen handles the temperature of your morning cup quite happily. Vitamin C largely does not. Tip a vitamin C blend into a hot drink and most of it degrades before it reaches anywhere useful. What you are left with is the taste, which is why some powders turn oddly citrussy, or get a flavour added to cover it.

And, the big one. Vitamin C does not help you absorb collagen. Absorption happens in your gut either way. Vitamin C’s role comes later, in your tissue, turning amino acids into structure over days. Not in your tea or coffee cup.

We care that the collagen information you come across is accurate. For more of the common myths and misconceptions, head to our journal and read 8 Frustrating Collagen Myths, Busted by Experts (link in bio).

Next time someone tells you vitamin C boosts collagen absorption, ask them to show you the study.

#collagen #collagenmyths

The spiral is nature’s most repeated shape. Found in the cochlea of the ear, the fern frond uncurling, the nautilus shell, the hurricane, the galaxy and your DNA.

The spiral has appeared in human history for centuries. Indeed, five thousand years ago, the builders of Newgrange carved it into stone and the ancient Celts understood it as the symbol of life, death and rebirth. 

It keeps appearing because it is the most elegant solution nature has found to a single problem: how to grow without losing where you came from. You expand outward but remain tethered to the centre. You return to the same themes; love, grief, the body, the seasons, purpose. 

Human life does not unfold in a straight line. It never was supposed to.

You are not going in circles. You are spiralling…. in the best way possible.

#spiral #nature #sacredgeometry #ancientandbrave

The Great Ascent ✨

The narrative around women and ageing can be a bleak one. That youth is the peak, that value fades as we get older, our bodies decline and we become irrelevant; even invisible to society. The good news? The scientific research tells a completely different story to what we’re told by this outdated trope.

Women aged 25 to 34 now hold more university degrees than men in over 55 countries. Meanwhile leadership research involving more than 11,000 people found that confidence increases with age and that women’s early confidence gap closes by midlife.

An analysis of 2.7 million founders found that successful entrepreneurs are more likely to be middle-aged than young. By 50, the odds of building a high-growth company are nearly twice what they are at 30.

And a meta-analysis following almost 165,000 people found that self-esteem rises throughout adulthood, reaching its highest point around 60 and remaining strong into the 70s.

More knowledge.
More confidence.
More meaningful experience.
More wonderful life to look forward to.

And your ‘70s? Well if Dame @helenmirren calls this decade “f***ing awesome”, then who are we to argue?

#Ageing #ancientandbrave #yourbecoming

A nourishing and balanced meal, perfect for dinner, and ideal for calming and relaxing the body after a long day. It contains high quality protein, it is rich in Omega-3s, Magnesium, B vitamins, and slow releasing carbohydrates - all of which help support healthy cortisol levels and ease the nervous system before bed.

Ingredients (serves 2):

2 wild caught trout fillets (or salmon)
Salt & black pepper, to taste
2 sweet potatoes
Dash of plant-based milk (I used almond milk)
3-4 generous handfuls of fresh spinach
2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp lemon juice
Small handful fresh parsley, finely chopped

Instructions:
Prepare the sweet potato mash: peel the sweet potatoes, cut them into 2-3cm chunks. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add a generous pinch of salt, and then add the sweet potatoes. Cook for 12-15min, or until the potatoes are soft when pierced with a fork. Drain and return to the pot or a medium sized bowl. Add a dash of plant based milk and a pinch of salt. Mash until smooth.

Cook the trout: season both trout fillet sides with salt and black pepper. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with some olive oil or butter. Place the trout skin-side down and cook for 3-4 minutes until the skin is crisp. Flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes, or until the flesh flakes gently. Remove the cooked trout from the pan, and add 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp of lemon juice, and chopped parsley to the pan for a few seconds.

Wilt the spinach: lightly saute the spinach for 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Necessary for building brain cells, DHA (a component of Omega-3) is essential for memory, focus, and overall brain function, making this delicious teriyaki salmon the perfect meal for days that require deep concentration.

Ingredients (for 2):
2 salmon fillets
2 portions rice noodles
2 baby pak choi
1 handful sugar snap peas
1 bell pepper (thinly sliced)
1 handful baby corn (halved)
1 tbsp olive oil

Teriyaki sauce:
3 tbsp soy sauce
2 tbsp honey
1–2 tsp rice vinegar
1 tsp garlic
1 tsp ginger
1 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water.

Method: Place the rice noodles in a bowl, cover with boiling water, and leave for 4–6 minutes (or according to packet instructions), then drain and set aside. To make the sauce, combine soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, and ginger in a small pan over gentle heat, then stir in the cornflour mix and simmer until glossy and slightly thickened. Cook the salmon to your liking. Stir-fry the vegetables in a pan or wok until just tender. Add the drained noodles, pour over the teriyaki sauce, and toss gently to combine. Enjoy! 🐟

Consider these Aphrodisia Bites pleasure, powered by nature.💕

Ingredients:
8-10 dates (optional: soaked in warm water)
¼ cup pumpkin seeds
2 tbsp almond butter
2 tbsp cacao powder
1 tbsp ground flaxseeds
½ tsp cinnamon
1 cup oats
Pinch of salt

Instructions:
Soak the dates. Place the dates in warm water for about 10min to soften them, then drain.
Blend the dry ingredients. In a food processor, combine the pumpkin seeds, cacao powder, ground flaxseeds, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. Pulse until the mixture is well combined.
Add the soaked dates to the food processor and blend again until the mixture starts to come together into a sticky dough.
Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl. Add the oats (gradually) and mix well to combine. Tip: if the mixture is too sticky, add a little more ground flaxseeds or oats.
Form the bites. Roll the mixture into small bowls and place them on a plate or into a glass food container. Refrigerate for at least 30min to firm up. Store in an airtight container in a fridge for up to a week.

These pumpkin seed bites are rich in zinc, healthy fats, and antioxidants, supporting testosterone production in men and hormone balance in women. Flaxseeds and almond butter help regulate oestrogen and provide building blocks for hormones, while cacao and cinnamon boost blood flow and sexual energy. Together, they make a tasty snack that naturally supports libido and overall hormonal health.

قالوا لك إن الكولاجين النباتي ما له وجود… وإنه ما يشتغل.
قالوا إن كولاجين السمك (المستخرج من جلد السمك) هو الخيار الوحيد.
بس الحقيقة؟ 👀

⚠️ كولاجين السمك رخيص في التصنيع، ويُباع بهامش ربح عالي جدًا.
⚠️ غالبًا جرعته ضعيفة، وامتصاصه سيئ، وتأثيره سلبي على المحيطات.

إحنا في فييل اخترنا طريق مختلف،
🌱 طريق مبني على العلم، مو على التنازلات.

فييل برو كولاجين
أول كولاجين نباتي في العالم مثبت فعاليته من خلال 4 دراسات سريريه.

✨ يقلل التجاعيد بنسبة ‎٢٢.٤٪ خلال ٤ أسابيع
✨ يزيد إنتاج جسمك الطبيعي للكولاجين بنسبة ‎١٣٥٪
✨ جزيئاته أصغر بـ ‎١٠٠ مرة لامتصاص أعلى
✨ يحتوي على نفس تركيبة الأحماض الأمينية الموجودة في الكولاجين البشري (النوع الأول) — الشيء اللي ما يقدر عليه لا البحري ولا الحيواني

ما في إيذاء للحيوانات.
ما في وعود فاضية.
بس في نتائج واضحة ومدعومة علميًا.

💜 لبشرة أحلى… وكوكب أنظف.
اضغطي الآن وخذي خصم ‎٢٠٪
جمالك ما يحتاج يضر الأرض.

You’ve probably never thought about putting collagen in your flatbread before. But hear us out…

We’ve joined forces with @ancientandbrave to bring you this no-bake, nutrient-dense Mediterranean flatbread. It’s the ultimate proof that you don’t have to separate your health rituals from your cooking practices. 

Packed with easily-digestible, highly-absorbable, and clinically-researched Type I hydrolysed bovine collagen peptides from their True Collagen and rich in heart-healthy antioxidants from our extra virgin olive oil, this is about to become your new favourite lunch ritual.

Ingredients for the flatbread:  
16g Citizens of Soil Olive oil (+ a drizzle to fry) 
20g Ancient + Brave True Collagen 200g Wholegrain flour 
60g Greek yogurt 
3G salt
115g water

Ingredients for the herby topping: 
2–3 tbsp Citizens of Soil EVOO (the Greek one from Sparta is great here!)
1–2 crushed garlic cloves (or 3g garlic powder) 
10g chopped fresh herbs  
10–15g mixed seeds 

Method: 
1. Mix the base: Combine the flour, True Collagen, and salt in a bowl. Add the yoghurt, olive oil, and water. Stir until a rough dough forms (add a splash of water if dry).

2. Knead & rest: Knead for 5 minutes until smooth and workable. Cover and let it rest for 30–45 minutes so the wholegrain flour hydrates perfectly.

3. Roll it out: On a floured surface, divide into 4 balls, flatten with your fingers, and roll out thin.

4. Pan-fry: Heat a drizzle of our olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook each flatbread for 1–2 minutes until bubbles form and the bottom browns, then flip for another 30–60 seconds.

5. Finish: Mix your topping ingredients in a small bowl, brush generously over the warm flatbread.

This is absolutely perfect for pairing with our trio of cupboard mezze dips (which you can find the exact recipes for in our Drizzle Cookbook!), roasted veggies, and halloumi. 

Seriously delicious. ✨

“My fish oil keeps repeating on me.” “I get fish oil burps hours after I take it” “I’ve given up on omega-3s, they all taste awful.” 🤢

I hear these in clinic all the time, and the reason behind them is simple 💡

In basic terms ➡️ in the same way properly fresh fish doesn’t taste fishy, fresh fish oil won’t either.

Omega-3 fats are delicate. Once they’re exposed to air, light or heat, they start to go off, in the same way any oil can turn rancid. 
As they break down, they create compounds which have a strong fishy taste and smell.
So a fishy fish oil is a sign it isn’t as fresh as it should be ❌

For some people digestion plays a part too. 
Lower stomach acid levels, which can happen when you’re busy, stressed, or have just exercised hard, means the oil sits in your stomach for longer. And then it’s more likely to come back up. 
Taking it during a meal that contains some fat will help it move through with your food to prevent that ✅

How often are you eating oily fish? 

This is a question I ask regularly to all my clients at any age, but especially in midlife. #AD

We can get some omega-3 from flax and chia seeds as ALA (alpha-linolenic acid), but while the amounts on the packaging look impressive, conversion into their active forms (DHA and EPA) is poor. 

Oily fish such as salmon, mackerel, anchovies, herring, sardines and sprats are rich sources of the active forms DHA and EPA. These are ready to work in the body and don’t need converting. Ideally, we want to be eating oily fish a few times a week, but many of us don’t manage that consistently. 

If you’re not a fan of fish, or if you are vegetarian, this can make it harder to consume sufficient omega-3 in the diet.

DHA and EPA are found in all of our cell membranes, with DHA being particularly concentrated in the brain and nervous tissue. We cannot make omega-3 from other fats, so we need to consume them in the diet.

Omega-3 matters at every age, but in midlife I pay extra attention to the heart, brain and eyes. EPA and DHA contribute to the normal function of the heart, and DHA contributes to the maintenance of normal brain and vision. 

I’ve recommended @barebiology Life & Soul fish oil capsules for many years in my clinic for their purity and high omega-3 levels per dose. Two capsules deliver 1700mg of total omega-3, with 1,100mg EPA and 500mg DHA, from wild-caught, sustainable fish.

It’s also certified by IFOS, the only International Fish Oil Standards, which is very important to me. 

If you’re vegetarian or vegan, they offer a Vim & Vigour, which is made from algae and contains DHA and EPA. 

We can get omega-3 into our diet in many ways, and I always take a food-first approach where possible. 

Breakfast: Adding 2 spoonfuls of flaxseeds or chia seeds to our porridge or yoghurt, or kippers!

Lunch: Smoked mackerel salad or a salmon poke bowl

Supper: Sardine puttanesca or a trout fillet with vegetables and green lentils. 

But if you need a helping hand, a reliable, high-quality supplement is a great way to meet your omega-3 needs consistently.

This is everything I want from an autumn dinner – cosy, creamy, comforting and seriously delicious. I've also added @wildnutritionltd Creatine + Collagen to make this dish work a little harder for you. AD

575kcal | 24g protein | 8g fibre per serving

Ingredients (serves 4)
* 700g butternut squash, peeled and deseeded
* 1 bulb garlic
* Mixed herbs and salt
* 1 tsp miso paste
* 250g ricotta
* Wild Nutrition Creatine Complex – 2 tsp per serving
* Wild Nutrition Collagen 500 Plus – 1 tsp per serving
* 1 tbsp olive oil
* Fresh sage leaves
* 1 leek
* 1 white onion
* 300g dry orzo
* 800ml vegetable stock
* 20g grated Parmesan
Method
1. Chop the squash into small chunks, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and mixed herbs.
2. Slice the top off the garlic bulb and roast alongside the squash at 180°C for 35–40 mins until golden and tender. Set aside half the squash for topping.
3. Blend the remaining squash with roasted garlic, ricotta, miso, Creatine and Collagen. Add around 100ml stock and blend until smooth.
4. Fry the sage in a little olive oil until crispy. Set aside, keeping the oil in the pan.
5. Add finely chopped onion and sliced leek. Cook until soft, then stir in the orzo.
6. Gradually add the vegetable stock, stirring regularly until the orzo is nearly cooked.
7. Stir in the squash sauce and simmer until creamy. Add Parmesan and cook until the orzo is tender and the sauce is thick and glossy.
8. Serve topped with roasted squash, crispy sage and extra spoonfuls of ricotta.
